title: Mine Eyes and My Desire
description: Mine Eyes and My Desire in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 25, part 3, headed “Distress of soul; or, Backsliding and desertion”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Mine eyes and my de-sire Are ev-er to the Lord; I love to plead his prom-is-es, And rest up-on his word.

lines: I love to plead his promises,
Turn, turn thee to my soul,
When will thy hand release my feet
Restore me from those dangerous ways
Look on my anguish and my pain,
Against my life they rise, and join
O keep my soul from death,
Nor put my hope to shame,
For I have plac'd my only trust
Of Israel it shall ne'er be said,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
